question: As a result of Green Revolution, import of food crops was _________ in India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**reduced.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Green Revolution in India led to an increase in domestic food production, reducing the need for imports.**
 
• Green Revolution was started in India in 1965-68.
 
• The green revolution is referred to as a period when Indian agriculture was converted into an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technologies.
 
• Indian agriculture made a transition from old and manual methods and new, innovative and technological methods.
 
• It included the use of products like High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers which were either not used or used on a very limited scale.
 
• The Indian Green Revolution was the brainchild of M.S. Swaminathan. 
 
• M.S. Swaminathan is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• This revolution led to an increase in food grain production especially in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Indian Green Revolution was a part of the larger and global Green Revolution started by Norman Borlaug.
 
• Norman Borlaug is called the Father of the Green Revolution in the world.
 
• Norman Borlaug was given the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for his contribution to saving over 1 billion people worldwide from dying of starvation.
